ordering.top_half: the timer top half may validate and enqueue fixed work, but worker dispatch is forbidden until the matching EOI epoch is observed
ordering.dispatch: each AP consumes only its private queue and executes one of two fixed typed payloads on its private guarded IST1 stack
ordering.cancellation: queued work becomes terminal immediately; remote in-flight cancellation records intent, accepts the exact AP acknowledgement, and discards the consumer result
ordering.rollback: an APIC-4 timeout restores the staged work to its source queue and rejects the late acknowledgement without consuming its result
ordering.fairness: high-priority work may bypass an available normal-priority item at most twice
ordering.flush_and_reclaim: the generation watermark must be terminal before slots are reclaimed, and stale generation-tagged work IDs are rejected
ordering.shutdown: all queues, dispatch tickets, and terminal slots drain before all three workers retire and 102 pages are scrubbed, verified, and released

nonclaims: PKSCHED5 supports only the frozen BSP-0/AP-1,2,3 legacy-xAPIC QEMU topology; it is not general topology, hotplug, NUMA, multi-socket, or x2APIC scheduling.
Only the fixed timer bottom-half and generation-reclaim payloads are added; arbitrary callbacks, function pointers, and dynamic worker registration are rejected.
The consumers are bounded kernel qualification consumers, not a complete production driver framework or service runtime.
No general SMP timer preemption, ring-3 task, address-space switch, or complete per-task architectural ownership is implemented.
No physical target, N12 exit, release, promotion, or production-readiness claim follows.
